- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.3), model often over-forecasts; reduce forecast to reflect bearish correction.  
- Model frequently over-estimates short-term spikes (e.g., +5–10% above recent high) and under-estimates subsequent mean reversion; apply a 1–2 day lag correction after sharp rises.  
- In periods of high volatility or sentiment swings, model tends to smooth out extremes; consider adding a 0.5–1.0 unit upward bias for the next 3–5 days if sentiment remains positive.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated low values (e.g., 0.0–0.33) over 5+ days, model under-forecasts; apply a 1–2% upward adjustment to avoid missing upward trend.  
- Model often under-forecasts the true 30-day mean; if historical 30-day average is > 65, adjust forecast to be at least 1–2 points above model output.  
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.33–0.67), model tends to be overly conservative; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5 units to reflect potential breakout.
